messages:
maya_docs: opened a small PR to tighten up Dedicated migration wording and add a Terraform quick example for tenant reservation + notes on what we don't guarantee (eviction/preemption behavior). link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/901
jon_infra: will review. can you paste the terraform snippet here so i can sanity-check resource names?
maya_docs: sure, pasted below — it's intentionally minimal to avoid implying we manage customer infra.

```hcl
# terraform snippet: request reserved capacity for tenant
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "tenant_acme" {
  tenant_id     = "acme-corp"
  gpu_count     = 4
  instance_type = "a10g"
  min_nodes     = 1
  max_nodes     = 4
  billing_plan  = "monthly-reserved"
  isolation     = "soft" # soft = best-effort isolation, hard = strict isolation
}
```

jon_infra: nice. tiny rename suggestion: use "reservation_type" instead of billing_plan to avoid confusion with billing docs.
maya_docs: good call, i'll update.
laura_pm: high-level: legal asked whether we're saying reserved pools are immune to preemption. We should be explicit: reserved pools reduce preemption probability but do not eliminate eviction during emergency maintenance.
niko_sre: agreed. suggest text: "Reserved pools provide prioritized placement and reduced preemption risk; in exceptional maintenance or unsafe hardware events, workloads may be migrated or evicted. We notify tenants and attempt graceful drain when possible."
hari_writer: I'll fold that into the SLA blurb. Also adding a short matrix that maps isolation: soft/hard -> implications (latency, cold starts, cache persistence).
maya_docs: here's the short matrix I added in the PR (as plain text):

- soft: shared shard, may be preempted; prefix cache best-effort; quicker autoscale; expected restart latency 1-5s for warm kernels.
- hard: dedicated shard, lower preemption risk; prefix cache persisted while node is live; restart latency 200-800ms for cold-started kernels.

jon_infra: numbers look plausible, but the hard latency seems optimistic for some model sizes. maybe phrase as ranges and add a note "depends on model and quantization".
maya_docs: done. changed wording to include that caveat.
laura_pm: another ask: update wording around "guaranteed throughput". We should avoid absolute guarantees for hosted variants. Use "target throughput" + SLA for Dedicated reserved commitments.
hari_writer: drafted sentence: "Target throughput and latency SLOs are published per-reservation tier; the service provides best-effort routing and prioritized placement for reserved pools. Reserved commitments include an uptime SLA subject to scheduled maintenance windows and emergency exceptions."
niko_sre: add pointer to runbook for emergency maintenance notifications.
maya_docs: linked runbook and added a short example of a migration playbook (one-liner) in the docs:

```bash
# migration playbook: graceful drain + fallback
redwoodctl drain --tenant acme-corp --timeout 300 && redwoodctl route-fallback --tenant acme-corp --variant lighter-bert
```

jon_infra: suggest adding a note that redwoodctl commands are operator-only and customers will see equivalent actions via the control plane UI/API.
maya_docs: added.
ci-bot: PR #901 tests passed (docs lint, linkcheck).
maya_docs: thanks! planning to merge after one more infra LGTM.
jon_infra: LGTM from infra. small nit on naming fixed.
ci-bot: PR #901 merged to main by maya_docs
maya_docs: merged. will send a quick changelog blurb and ping customer success to update migration checklist. :rocket:
